description: The bar chart illustrates a comparison of execution accuracy between two Text-to-SQL models — NatSQL and TA-SQL — across three query difficulty levels (Simple, Moderate, Challenging) and an overall Total score. The vertical axis, labeled “Execution Accuracy,” ranges from 20 to 60, with tick marks at intervals of 10. The horizontal axis categorizes the data into four groups: Simple, Moderate, Challenging, and Total. For each category, two adjacent bars represent the two models: NatSQL (light blue) and TA-SQL (dark blue), as indicated by the legend in the upper right. In the Simple category, TA-SQL achieves 63.14% accuracy, outperforming NatSQL’s 60.21%. In Moderate, TA-SQL scores 48.60% versus NatSQL’s 39.64%. In Challenging, TA-SQL again leads with 36.11% compared to NatSQL’s 32.32%. The Total score shows TA-SQL at 56.19% and NatSQL at 51.35%. Across all categories, TA-SQL consistently outperforms NatSQL, with the largest gap observed in the Moderate category (8.96 percentage points). The chart visually emphasizes TA-SQL’s superior performance, particularly on more complex queries, supporting the paper’s claim that its alignment strategy effectively mitigates hallucinations in Text-to-SQL generation.
